summary: void snapshots.save() swallows disk write failures silently — critical run history data may be lost
evidence: run handler line 284: `void snapshots.save(...)` — same pattern at lines 316, 397, 414, 507, 520. All terminal event branches use `void` to fire-and-forget snapshot persistence. If the filesystem is full (ENOSPC), permission-denied (EACCES), or the workflow-runs dir has been manually deleted (ENOENT), the rejection is swallowed by `void` with no catch and no user-visible feedback. Snapshot loss means the run history dialog shows nothing and runner hydration from disk (line 567) returns null, rendering the run effectively invisible.
suggestedFix: Either `await` the save (at the cost of delaying the IPC response) or add `.catch((err) => logger.error(...))` so failures are at least logged. The log-store already captures main-process errors.
